name: A 'Sea-God', Naples
bio: A young man Wilde met during a three-day stop at Naples on his Italian journey of April 1900, and with whom, in his own words to Robert Ross, he 'fell in love'. Wilde calls him a Sea-God and says he was at the Regia Marina School - the Italian naval school - 'instead of being with Triton'. No name, age, dates or further trace appear on the page read.
bio_note: Sole source: Wilde to Robert Ross, 16 April [1900], c/o Cook & Son, Piazza di Spagna, Rome, Complete Letters (2000), p. 1179 (PDF 1225, printed folio 1179 confirmed at the foot of the rendered page image). What is verified in the source: the editors' footnote 2 on the same page reads 'Easter Day 1900 was on 15 April', and Wilde places his Vatican appearance 'yesterday', which is consistent with the mirror's 16 April heading.
